mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over the prior three months signals a tightening monetary regime, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, which drives negative S&P 500 forward 20-day returns.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% per month for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a softening labor market (UNRATE < 5%) signals weakening aggregate demand, which depresses corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the mean return is not significantly below zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained acceleration in industrial production (INDPRO) above its 12-month moving average by more than 1.5% signals improving supply capacity and corporate earnings momentum, which drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: INDPRO acceleration is present but S&P 500 20-day returns are not statistically higher than baseline in at least 70% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) of at least 50,000 coincident with a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4.5% signals a tight labor market, which raises wage inflation and input costs, ultimately leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as profit margins compress.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not significantly below zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A two-month decline in the Housing Starts Index (HOUST) of more than 10% signals weakening residential investment and consumer confidence, which reduces GDP growth and corporate sales, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST falls by >10% over any two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both CPIAUCSL (CPI) and FEDFUNDS by more than 0.5% in the same month signals a dual shock of higher inflation and tighter policy, which increases real interest rates and depresses equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL > 0.5% AND FEDFUNDS > 0.5% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered months, or the mean return is not significantly below zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly contraction in the Industrial Production Index (INDPRO) below its 6-month moving average by more than 1% signals deteriorating manufacturing activity and earnings pressure, which leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 6-month moving average by >1% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid deceleration in nonfarm payrolls growth (PAYEMS month-over-month change falling by at least 100,000 in one month) while the unemployment rate (UNRATE) rises by more than 0.3 percentage points signals a sudden labor market weakening, which foreshadows negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS MoM change drops by ≥100,000 AND UNRATE rises by >0.3pp in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are not significantly negative in at least 70% of triggered months.
